learningObjective: Explain what AOTInductor produces (a self-contained shared library that runs a compiled PyTorch model without a Python runtime) and how that differs from torch.compile in JIT mode.
stem: Which statement best describes what AOTInductor produces and how it differs from the default JIT torch.compile flow?

options.text: AOTInductor ahead-of-time compiles an exported PyTorch model into a self-contained shared library (plus the generated kernels) that can be loaded and invoked from C++ without a Python interpreter or the Inductor compiler present at runtime; JIT torch.compile compiles on first call and requires Python + Inductor at run time.
AOTInductor is a re-implementation of the CUDA driver API; it lets torch.compile bypass cuBLAS and cuDNN by JIT-compiling all matmuls on the fly at each inference call.

AOTInductor is a smaller runtime that replaces Python entirely; it JIT-compiles PyTorch models at process start using an embedded MicroPython interpreter, producing the same kernels as torch.compile but launching them from within a compiled binary.

AOTInductor produces a Python-only artifact (a `.pyc` file) that still requires Python at runtime; the only difference from JIT torch.compile is that graph capture happens ahead of time while codegen happens on the first call.

explanation: AOTInductor is the AOT compilation path for torch.compile: given an `torch.export`-produced graph, AOTInductor emits a shared library (.so) containing the generated kernels and a C-ABI entry point. The library is deployable without Python and without the Inductor compiler at run time. JIT torch.compile, by contrast, compiles lazily and depends on Python + Inductor at the deployment site.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: matches the AOTInductor design as described in the PyTorch docs.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: AOTInductor does not replace CUDA driver APIs.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: no embedded Python interpreter; it is a native artifact.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: it is not a .pyc; it is a native shared library.

nonImplications: Does not imply AOTInductor supports every torch.compile feature; some dynamic behaviors are restricted.
Does not imply zero build cost; users trade first-call latency for offline build time.
